# Gap Matrix — 028 Review-Finding Liveness, Phase 01

**Phase**: `phase-01` — Regression guards for the landed W1/W2 contract
**Generated by**: `/gwrk-define-tests`
**Test files**: 1 created, 1 amended

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This phase's tests are GREEN by design, not RED.** Phase 01 adds no production code — the plan
> is explicit: *"No production code changes: if any assertion here fails, W1/W2 have regressed on
> `develop` and that is the finding."* FR-001…FR-007 already landed (`a57a68f`, `e588d1f`, PR #176);
> this phase converts them from historical fact into executable contract. The RED tests for this
> feature belong to Phases 02–06 (TR-008…TR-012) and are deliberately **not** authored here: every
> phase gate from 01 to 05 runs `ship-orchestrator.review-finding-liveness.test.ts` bare and requires
> exit 0, so landing a Phase-02 assertion now would make Phases 01–05 ungateable.
>
> The guards were verified to have teeth by replaying each assertion against the pre-fix sources
> (`a57a68f^` for the prompts, `e588d1f^` for the orchestrator): **11/11 representative prompt guards
> and both TR-007 guards fire on the defective input**. See § Anti-hollowness verification.

### One spec-authored assertion was corrected

US-007 AS-2 and VR-006 word the TR-007 negative guard as:

```
! grep -q 'If any tasks in the phase are .open. .* NO-GO' src/engine/ship-orchestrator.ts
```

The sentence it targets, verbatim from `e588d1f^`, is:

```
If any tasks in the phase are "open", the review agent re-opened them → NO-GO.
```

`.open.` consumes `"open"`, after which the pattern requires a **space** — but the text has a comma.
The pattern matches nothing in either direction, so as an assertion it can only ever pass: it would
not notice a byte-for-byte restoration of the sentence it exists to forbid. That is the same
false-green shape as the defect under repair, so the test uses a corrected form
(`/If any tasks? in the phase (?:are|is) .open.[\s\S]{0,160}NO-GO/`) which was verified to fire on
`e588d1f^` and not on the current source. The reasoning is recorded in the test body.

Two related traps the plan already documented and this phase inherits: `! grep -q` is exempt from
`set -e` and can never fail a gate, and `vitest run <file> -t "<case>"` exits 0 when nothing matches.
The phase gates use the `if grep …; then exit 1; fi` form and assert named-case existence with a
bare `grep -q` against the test source.
